question.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $x.$ To do this, we treat $y$ as though it were a constant and apply the addition and multiplication principles as usual.

First, we add $5y$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}-5y & =2y \\ \frac{x}{2}-5y+5y & =2y+5y \\ \frac{x}{2} & =2y+5y \\ \frac{x}{2} & =7y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we multiply both sides of the equation by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & =7y \\ 2\cdot \frac{x}{2} & =2\cdot 7y \\ \cancel{2}\cdot \frac{x}{\cancel{2}} & =2\cdot 7y \\ x & =2\cdot 7y \\ x & =14y\end{aligned}
$$
